newsitem.title: USA: Cano Limon delays seen in busy foreign crude day.
newsitem.headline: Cano Limon delays seen in busy foreign crude day.

text.p: Loadings of Colombian Cano Limon crude oil were expected to be delayed by two to three days as a result of back-to-back rebel bombings of the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline, traders said on Thursday.
The blasts paralyzed the 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) pipeline, leaving all storage capacity full. As a result, operator Occidental has shut in production of around 200,000 bpd.
The shutdown gave domestic sour grades a brief respite on Thursday afternoon, traders said.
The flurry over Cano Limon was only one dimension of a busy foreign crude market. Several foreign grades were heard placed, although details remained sketchy.
"There's some buying interest as people try to fill august holes," said one Gulf Coast dealer.
Equity producer Total sold a Cusiana cargo loading August 16-20 at an unconfirmed discount to West Texas Intermediate/Cushing of around 80-85 cents a barrel fob.
The grade was last sold at minus 85 cents.
Out of Asia, a trading house was heard to have placed an Indonesian Widuri cargo, while a U.S. refiner sold Tapis and Labuan to a Houston refiner, traders said.
The prices could not be immediately confirmed, although the Widuri had been offered at WTI minus $1.30 a barrel delivered.
Finally, Brent remained on offer for mid- to late August arrival around WTI minus 25 cents a barrel, up five to 10 cents from recent days, traders said.
